name: India ↔ Gulf Maritime Route
genZNote: This is India's most-used sea route and it's basically an energy lifeline — most of the oil that keeps the country running arrives this way.

sections.heading: 🛳️ Route Path
bullets: Gulf ports (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq) → Strait of Hormuz → Arabian Sea → Indian west-coast ports (Mumbai/JNPT, Mundra, Kandla, Kochi).
One of the shortest and most heavily used of India's international maritime routes because of its geographic proximity.

sections.heading: 📦 Why It Matters
bullets: Carries the bulk of India's crude oil and LNG imports.
Also a major route for Indian exports of refined petroleum products, engineering goods, and food products moving the other way toward the Gulf.
The Gulf region is also home to a very large Indian expatriate population, which drives significant passenger and remittance-linked economic activity alongside cargo trade.
India-UAE and India-Saudi Arabia trade relationships are heavily built on this maritime corridor.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The India-Gulf maritime route connects India's west coast to Gulf ports via the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Sea, carrying most of India's oil imports.
keyFacts: Path: Gulf ports → Strait of Hormuz → Arabian Sea → India's west coast.
India's primary crude oil and LNG import route.
Major Indian export route for refined petroleum and engineering goods.
Underpins large Gulf-India expatriate and remittance flows.
commonConfusion: This route is distinct from India's Southeast Asia route — different ocean side of India (west coast/Arabian Sea vs. east coast/Bay of Bengal).

highYieldFacts: India-Gulf route passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Primary route for India's oil/LNG imports.
Key ports: JNPT, Mundra, Kandla (India side).
commonTraps: Don't confuse this route's chokepoint (Hormuz) with the Southeast Asia route's chokepoint (Malacca).
mustRemember: India-Gulf route = India's energy lifeline via the Arabian Sea and Strait of Hormuz.
